title: Completion of coherent modules is an exact functor
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] whose underlying space is quasi-compact) and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. The category $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)$ of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent] and the category $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] are abelian [def-sp-abelian] ([lem-weil-pbc-abelian-full-subcategory-exact], [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian]), and the completion functor $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)\to\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (2), $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F^\wedge=(\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)_{n\ge1}$, $u\mapsto u^\wedge=(u\bmod\mathcal I^n)_n$, is exact: it is additive and carries every short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$ of $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)$ to a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F'^\wedge\to\mathcal F^\wedge\to\mathcal F''^\wedge\to0$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] (for an additive functor between abelian categories this is Stacks' 'exact', i.e. commuting with finite limits and finite colimits, by Homology, Lemma 010N (4)).

proof.text: The coherent inclusion preserves epimorphisms because it creates cokernels. For an epi f, each quotient reduction is epi: its composite with the quotient projection is f followed by the target quotient projection, a composite of epis. All components of the completed natural transformation are epi; its full inclusion reflects epimorphisms. Thus completion preserves epis without using the formal first-component criterion.

proof.text: For the mapped complex T of a short exact S, T.g is epi by the preceding step. Apply the existing local short-exactness criterion to the cover of all affine opens. On each affine U the new affine kernel theorem supplies IsLimit of the first-arrow fork; Fork.IsLimit.mono gives its mono and exact_of_f_is_kernel gives middle exactness. Homology is obtained from the abelian witness after transporting the unique zero-morphism structure.

proof.text: To obtain the local epi, form the canonical kernel sequence of the global epi T.g. This is short exact by the kernel universal property. Restriction preserves this short exact sequence by the local exactness theorem; its second arrow is precisely the restriction of T.g. Combine local exactness, mono and epi by ShortExact.mk', and use the covering criterion to conclude that T is globally short exact.
